name: RT-2 Vision-Language-Action Models (technique summary + current tooling)
observations: Source: Brohan et al. 2023, 'RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control' (Google DeepMind, arXiv:2307.15818v1), 26-page PDF read in full text for pp.1-12; project page robotics-transformer2.github.io.

Core idea: treat robot actions as 'another language'. A continuous action vector is discretized into integer bins and emitted as ordinary text tokens, so a pretrained VLM can be trained on robot trajectories with NO new architecture or action-specific layers — model weights are fully shared between language/VQA tasks and action prediction. This class of model is called a VLA (vision-language-action) model.

Action encoding (from RT-1 protocol): 8 integers per step = 6-DoF end-effector Delta-position + Delta-rotation, gripper extension, plus a discrete 'terminate' episode command. All continuous dims are uniformly discretized into 256 bins. Target is a space-separated string, e.g. 'terminate dposx dposy dposz drotx droty drotz gripper' -> '1 128 91 241 5 101 127'.

Token mapping is tokenizer-dependent: PaLI-X has unique tokens for integers up to 1000 so bins map directly to integer tokens; PaLM-E lacks this, so the 256 least-frequently-used tokens are overwritten to serve as the action vocabulary (a form of symbol tuning).

Training data format: inputs are robot camera image(s) + instruction in VQA style ('Q: what action should the robot take to [instruction]? A:'), output is the numeric action string. Trained on RT-1's robot demonstrations (13 robots, 17 months, office kitchen) mixed with web-scale VQA/captioning data.

Key recipe detail — co-fine-tuning: mixing the original web vision-language data into robot fine-tuning beats fine-tuning on robot data alone, because the model does not forget web-learned visual/semantic concepts. Robot data is up-weighted in each batch to balance the mixture. Ablations: training from scratch performs very poorly even at 5B; co-fine-tuning > robot-only fine-tuning > from scratch at every size, and larger models generalize better.

Decoding constraint: when prompted with a robot-action task, sample only from the valid action-token vocabulary so outputs are always executable; on standard VLM tasks the full natural-language vocabulary remains available.

Instantiations: RT-2-PaLI-X at 5B and 55B (PaLI-X backbone), RT-2-PaLM-E at 12B (PaLM-E backbone). Roughly 6,000 real-robot evaluation trajectories across seen tasks and unseen objects/backgrounds/environments.

Results: on seen tasks RT-2 matches RT-1; on generalization it is ~2x better than the next best baselines (RT-1, MOO) and ~6x better than others (VC-1, R3M). Emergent abilities from web pretraining: symbol understanding ('move apple to 3', 'push coke can on top of heart'), visual/math/multilingual reasoning ('move X near the sum of two plus one', 'mueve la manzana al vaso verde'), and human recognition ('move the coke can to the person with glasses') — best model >3x RT-1 average on these. Simulated Language-Table benchmark: RT-2-PaLI-3B 90±10 vs LAVA 77±4, RT-1 74±13, BC-Zero 72±3.

Chain-of-thought variant: a few hundred gradient steps of fine-tuning on data augmented with a 'Plan:' field in natural language before the 'Action:' tokens (e.g. 'Instruction: I'm hungry. Plan: pick rxbar chocolate. Action: 1 128 124 136 121 158 111 255'), which bridges VQA reasoning and manipulation and enables multi-stage semantic inference (improvised hammer -> rock; tired person -> energy drink).

Real-time inference: 55B models cannot run on robot GPUs, so RT-2 is served as a multi-TPU cloud service queried over the network; 55B runs at ~1-3 Hz and the 5B at ~5 Hz, with one service driving multiple robots.

Limitations stated by the authors: physical skills remain bounded by the robot-data distribution (web pretraining transfers semantics, not new motions); compute cost makes high-frequency control the main bottleneck (quantization/distillation suggested); few VLMs are openly fine-tunable for building VLAs.

Current best-practice tooling (Context7, Hugging Face LeRobot v0.6.1): SmolVLA is the open VLA implementation — `lerobot-train --policy.type=smolvla --policy.load_vlm_weights=true --dataset.repo_id=... --steps=... --batch_size=...`, or fine-tune a pretrained base with `--policy.path=lerobot/smolvla_base` (~4h for 20k steps on one A100, batch 64).

LeRobot parameter-efficient path: LoRA fine-tuning of SmolVLA via `--peft.method_type=LORA --peft.r=64 --peft.lora_alpha=64` with learning rate ~1e-3 (about 10x full fine-tuning) and scheduler decay 1e-4.

LeRobot also ships built-in eval harnesses (`--env.type=libero|libero_plus|robocasa|vlabench`, `--env.task=...`, `--env_eval_freq`, `--eval.n_episodes`) and `push_to_hub`/`policy.repo_id` for sharing checkpoints — directly analogous to RT-2's closed-loop evaluation methodology.

LeRobot async inference solves exactly RT-2's real-time-serving problem in open source: `python -m lerobot.async_inference.policy_server --host=0.0.0.0 --port=8080 --fps=30` on the GPU host plus `python -m lerobot.async_inference.robot_client --server_address=<host>:8080 --policy_type=smolvla --actions_per_chunk=50 --chunk_size_threshold=0.5 --aggregate_fn_name=weighted_average` on the robot, so only action chunks cross the network and control loops stay on-device.

HF Transformers side (Context7 docs): the relevant building blocks are multimodal ProcessorMixin classes (e.g. PaliGemma = SigLIP image processor + Llama tokenizer) and AutoModelForImageTextToText/AutoProcessor with chat templates and `generate(...)`; these give the VLM backbone and tokenizer needed for a tokenized-action VLA. No RT-2-specific model class surfaced in the queried Transformers docs, so reimplementing RT-2's 256-bin action-token scheme on a PaliGemma-class backbone would be custom work rather than a documented API.

name: LeRobot (Hugging Face robotics library)
observations: Context7 ID /huggingface/lerobot, docs version v0.6.1, high source reputation, very large code-snippet coverage.

Provides end-to-end robot learning: datasets on the Hub, policy training CLI (lerobot-train), simulation eval harnesses (LIBERO, LIBERO-plus, RoboCasa, VLABench), PEFT/LoRA support, and async inference (policy server + robot client over gRPC).
Policies include SmolVLA (VLA), pi05, and ACT; checkpoints are pushed to and loaded from the Hugging Face Hub.

name: Hugging Face Transformers
observations: Context7 IDs include /huggingface/transformers and /llmstxt/huggingface_co_transformers_v5_2_0_llms_txt.

Relevant for VLA work as the source of vision-language backbones (PaliGemma = SigLIP + Llama), ProcessorMixin multimodal preprocessors, AutoProcessor/chat templates, and AutoModelForImageTextToText generation APIs.
Queried docs contain no RT-2-specific VLA model class or action-tokenizer API; action discretization must be implemented on top of a general VLM.
